title: The Knit Degree of a Finite Inverse Semigroup
content: Paulista asked whether a finite inverse semigroup can have knit degree greater than one. We prove that every defined knit degree of a finite inverse semigroup is one or two, and construct a degree-two inverse semigroup of order sixteen. The proof first isolates a two-edge chain: shorter chains force the endpoints of a left path to form a left edge, while longer chains already generate one. A cyclic component of order at least three prevents the remaining construction from admitting a left edge. Its generated inverse semigroup has thirteen nonempty chain restrictions and one element for each cyclic power. This description proves that sixteen is the least possible order for a degree-two inverse semigroup and that the example of this order is unique up to isomorphism. The main spectrum, minimum-order, and uniqueness results are verified in Lean.
